as_told.title: Rumsfeld's $2.3 trillion in unaccounted Pentagon spending

plain: The claim is that in 2001, the day before the September 11 attacks, Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld publicly admitted that the Pentagon could not account for trillions of dollars. A journalist named Ross Coulthart tells Michels he dug up Rumsfeld's speech while writing his book, and that in it Rumsfeld "admitted that there was something" wrong with the books. A researcher named Richard Dolan tells it too, from memory and without a single source. He says the first figure was "2.3 trillion dollars in unaccounted expenditures" and that Rumsfeld kept revising it. Dolan sets it before the House Armed Services Committee over 2001 and 2002, and links the figure to two people he names, Dov Zakheim and Catherine Austin Fitts. Both men tell it for the same reason: if it is true, vast sums were moving through the Pentagon outside any normal accounting, money that could pay for programmes nobody sees.
